meta.title: NYS Senate campaign donor snapshot
meta.sourceAgency: New York State Board of Elections
methodology: Only monetary contribution Schedules A, B and C in itemized disclosure filings; transaction date 2025-01-01 through 2026-11-22, disclosure year at least 2025.

Amended filings are retained. Repeated UUID transaction IDs retain the latest filing_trans_id; legacy numeric transaction IDs are deduplicated only when filer, schedule, date, amount and disclosed donor name/type also agree, since numeric IDs can be reused.

Donor ranks aggregate the same disclosed donor name (case and whitespace normalized) and contributor type within the displayed candidate/committee group. Distinct people with the same disclosed name may be combined; name spelling variants are not inferred to be one person.

Totals are gross disclosed monetary contributions, not net receipts or cash on hand. Unitemized/unnamed contributions are included in the total when reported but excluded from named donor rankings. Subsequent refunds to contributors are not netted out.

Loans, transfers, in-kind support, independent expenditures and public matching funds are outside these donor rankings. Identifiable Comptroller public funds and transaction narratives explicitly describing recovered bank balances, bank verification credits, dividends, expense refunds, payroll-provider balance returns or reimbursements were excluded even when filed in contribution schedules.

Candidate-to-committee identities use official filer names, candidate office/district records and, where available, explicit official PCFB payment-report mappings. The mapping basis is retained per candidate.
No residential addresses, emails, telephone numbers, employer addresses or treasurer personal details are included.
Source filings are reported by campaigns and may be amended. Missing data is not a zero-donation claim.

notes: Freshly retrieved Census-origin estimates, not values copied from the project handoff.

Single-cell estimates and margins of error are published values. Summed/differenced counts use approximate root-sum-square margins of error.
Derived percentages use the Census subset-proportion MOE approximation; a negative variance term falls back to the ratio formula. Derived MOEs are approximate and do not include full covariance.
High sampling uncertainty means a coefficient of variation greater than 30% using SE = MOE / 1.645. This is a presentation flag, not a Census suppression rule.
Null is missing/suppressed; an estimated zero is retained with its margin of error. No missing value is filled with zero.
No demographic table establishes religious affiliation, political preferences, individual eligibility to vote, or donor identity.

meta.title: Official NYC neighborhood and election-district overlays for NY Senate districts
meta.boundaryVersion: NYC 26c, updated 2026-11-02; NTA statistical definitions are 2020 vintage
meta.method: Official NYC polygons projected and spatially clipped to matching NYC DCP 26c State Senate district polygons. The statewide atlas projection is retained exactly, while the detailed NYC Senate outline avoids mismatched shared edges from separately generalized statewide data. NTA fragments below 100 m², ED fragments below 1 m², or fragments below 0.1% of source feature area are suppressed; the lower ED threshold retains all 4,214 published precinct geometries, including very small shoreline features. SVG display simplified 5 m for NTAs and 3 m for EDs, preserving topology; areas calculated before simplification. Label points lie inside clipped polygons.
limits: Neighborhood tabulation areas approximate neighborhoods; they are statistical areas, not definitive neighborhood borders.
Detailed overlays use the matching NYC DCP 26c Senate, NTA and ED representations. At transition from the statewide atlas, tiny outline differences can occur due to the atlas service generalization.
An ED can intersect multiple Senate districts. The clip does not allocate voters, population, or votes.
No election returns are supplied or inferred by this geometry dataset.
Non-NYC Senate districts are outside the coverage of these NYC datasets.
